reason: As written the falsifier is mis-specified, but it can be repaired into a cheap, sharp test that will very likely FALSIFY hypothesis (a). (1) Algebra: F_i = Tr(w_i u), so 1 in the F_2 ideal iff 1 = Tr(u*h) for some K-valued h of degree <= d-2 (h = sum w_i g_i), whereas 1 in the one-generator K-closure iff u*h = 1, i.e. h = 1/u pointwise on the cube. Tr(uh)=1 is one F_2-linear condition per point; uh=1 is n of them. So d_K = degree of the multilinear interpolant of 1/u, computable EXACTLY by one Moebius transform over 2^N points, no elimination. For an unsat (nowhere-zero) generic u this interpolant has full degree N=2k, while d_F <= k+2. Smoke test (my own, python3, GF(2^n) tables, u = (sum a_j v_j)(sum b_l w_l) + K-linear(a,b) + kappa with random v,w,c,e, nowhere-zero kappa; NOT the true Semaev u, so structural only): n=5,k=3 gives d_K=6=N, Nullstellensatz d_F=4 and 3 on two seeds; n=7,k=4 and n=9,k=5 runs did not finish in 120 s because my F_2 Gram step was naive, no result. So the predicted gap d_K-d_F ~ N/2 grows with k, contradicting (a) 'gap <= 1', and (b) 'd_K >= c*k' becomes trivially true (d_K=N) and carries no information about d_F. (2) Control/discrimination: the stated if_true/if_false predictions are separated only if d_K is observable below the cap; with cap 5-6 and N=10..18, d_K is right-censored (>cap) at every instance while d_F is not, so every instance lands in 'false' (gap >= 2) and 'd_K increases 4->5->6' is unobservable. No null arm: need random-u control (random F_2-structured degree-2 K-polynomial with the same support, not Semaev-derived) and a 'planted-satisfiable' control (u with a zero) to show the pipeline reports no refutation; neither is specified. (3) Runnability: stated size '5e4 rows x 3.1e4 cols over F_{2^17}' in pure python is infeasible (~1e13 field ops). Realistic: N=18, deg 5 gives 988 rows x 12616 cols, ~1e10 mults, feasible only with numpy log/exp-table vectorised row ops (~1-3 min); deg 6 (4048 x 31180, ~2.5e11) is not feasible in 20 CPU-min. The 'rounds until stable' fall iteration also multiplies cost. (4) Scaling to n=131: nothing in the toy transfers except the structural statement 'u*h=1 forces full-degree interpolant of 1/u while Tr(uh)=1 does not', which is a proof-level argument that applies at any n (1/u over 2^132 points is generic full degree); so the toy at best illustrates a general counting fact, and the F_2-closure d_F toy values stay toy-only. Hypothesis (a) in effect says one conjugate suffices; the count above says the n conjugates are the entire content (descent from K to F_2 loses n-1 of n equations per point). (5) Metrics: dimension/rank/degree quantities, not wall time: fine.
fix: Replace the elimination-based design by: (i) exact d_K = max |S| over S with nonzero Moebius coefficient of 1/u on {0,1}^N, via numpy int tables for GF(2^n), n=9..21 odd, N=2k=n+1<=22 (2^22 points x 22 passes ~ seconds); report d_K/N across n and across 30 true Semaev-derived unsat instances plus the random-u control and a planted-zero control (u with a root: no inverse, report 'not refutable'). (ii) d_F by the existing F_2 closure/Nullstellensatz machinery (idea 1 arm A) at n<=17, and by the Tr(uh)=1 reformulation: solve for h in the K-space of degree-e functions with Tr(u h)=1 on all points, as ONE F_2-linear system with n*C(N,<=e) unknowns and 2^N equations (cheap, N<=18). (iii) Replace the 'conjugate-pair closure {u,sigma u}' with the family {u, sigma^{j} u : j in J} for |J|=1,2,4,n/2,n and record d_J versus |J| (the interpolating-degree analogue: need h_J with sum_{j in J} sigma^j(u h_j)=1); this directly measures whether cross-conjugate falls are bounded. (iv) Redefine prediction: if_true = d_K <= d_F+1 and d_J flat in |J| beyond |J|=2; if_false = d_K = N (full) with d_F <= k+2, expected outcome, and |J| required for d_J=d_F grows with n. Record also dim ratio n*dim_K V^K_d / dim_F2 W_d (an upper bound; ratio >> 1 means conjugates overlap). Budget ~5 CPU-min. If outcome as predicted, hypothesis (a) is refuted and the reduction to a one-generator problem is dead; keep only (iii) as a diagnostic for how many conjugates the low-degree refutation uses.
